day_shape: 113 items: UN Security Council emergency session on Iranian drones hitting UAE's Barakah nuclear plant, fresh US Treasury/State sanctions on Iranian currency networks and 19 vessels, US Senate advances Iran war-powers measure, NYT reports Israeli plan to install Ahmadinejad, CENTCOM claims 89 vessels redirected under blockade.

threads.label: Barakah nuclear plant drone strike fallout
threads.summary: The IAEA Director General told an emergency UN Security Council meeting that Iranian drones striking the Barakah Nuclear Power Plant narrowly averted a nuclear disaster, with the UAE Defense Ministry reporting six drones launched from Iraq in 48 hours. Iraq publicly distanced itself from Iran-backed militias and condemned the attacks.

threads.label: US sanctions and blockade enforcement
threads.summary: The State Department announced sanctions on Iranian currency exchange houses, associated front companies and 19 vessels under the Economic Fury campaign, plus separate designations targeting Hamas support networks and a Gaza flotilla leader. CENTCOM said 89 commercial vessels have been redirected under the US blockade of Iranian ports, and Treasury Secretary Bessent called on allies to target Iran's shadow banking.

threads.label: US-Iran war-resumption diplomacy
threads.summary: The US Senate advanced a measure curbing Trump's Iran war powers nearly along party lines, while VP Vance said significant progress had been made in talks but escalation would serve US interests absent a deal. Israeli officials told the Jerusalem Post they believe Trump will eventually strike, and the NYT reported Israeli-developed war plans sought to install Mahmoud Ahmadinejad to lead Iran after Khamenei's killing.

threads.label: Strait of Hormuz and Gulf risk
threads.summary: A US intelligence assessment cited by CBS identified at least 10 mines planted by Iran in the Strait of Hormuz, while Iran International reported Tehran floating 'protection fees' for subsea fibre-optic cables there. Gulf states reportedly urged Trump to delay strikes citing risks to desalination, oil, and shipping routes.

threads.label: Regime defiance and Khamenei messaging
threads.summary: Khamenei's office published a sequence of letters tying Iran's post-war 'power' to population growth, while President Pezeshkian said Iran would not surrender to economic blockade and the IRGC warned regional war would extend beyond the region if aggression resumed. IRIB carried a joint Xi-Putin statement claimed to condemn US and Israeli attacks on Iran as violations of international law.

threads.label: Lebanon and Gaza front incidents
threads.summary: The IDF announced Maj (res.) Itamar Sapir, 27, deputy commander of Battalion 7008, was killed in an exchange of fire with Hezbollah in southern Lebanon. The IDF also intercepted all ships in a Gaza-bound flotilla, transferring over 400 activists to Israel, and said a southern Gaza strike killed a Hamas operative who took part in 7 October.

threads.label: Iranian economy and mobilisation
threads.summary: The Tehran Stock Exchange reopened after an 80-day shutdown under heavy state controls with 42 major firms still suspended, per Iran International. Times of Israel and Jerusalem Post reported Iran staging mass weddings for couples pledging 'sacrificial service' in war with the US and Israel.

events.summary_en: Xi and Putin condemn US and Israeli attacks on Iran. The statement said: 'Both sides agree that the military attacks by the United States and Israel on Iran violate international law and the fundamental principles of international relations and seriously undermine stability in the Middle East.' events.summary_en: 50 per cent increase in price of military equipment in Europe. The Bloomberg news agency reported: the Defence Minister of Estonia warned that European countries, due to increased global demand and severe shortage of raw materials, have faced a 50 per cent increase in the costs of purchasing weapons and defence equipment. This jump in prices has confronted the efforts of EU member states to rebuild and strengthen their military capabilities in the shadow of new security threats with serious financial challenges. The delivery time of military orders has also become unprecedentedly long, and some countries must wait years to receive basic ammunition.
